page.summary: Prioritize a safe heal on a teammate with hook-state danger; Do No Harm scales only with the target's Hook States while you heal them.

verdict.recommendation: Treat the new 10.2.0 healing values as an experimental triage option, not proof that every injured teammate should be chased down.
verdict.soloQ: Confirm the target is reachable and has a Hook State before leaving an urgent objective or rescue.
verdict.coordinatedSwf: Assign one healer to the endangered player and keep the other jobs covered; call when pressure makes the reset unsafe.
verdict.mainWeakness: The perk adds nothing for a zero-Hook-State target and cannot repay a long, unsafe trip to heal.

options.whyItsHere: While healing another Survivor, each of their Hook States adds 30/35/40% heal speed, 3% progress on Great basic healing checks and 5% check occurrence chance.

item.name: Med-Kit
item.why: Optional finite healing resource; the hook-state scaling comes from Do No Harm, not the item.

opening: Check the injured player's hook-state danger, travel cost and whether the Killer has left a safe reset window.

rows.situation: An injured teammate with one or two Hook States is reachable and a heal can protect their next chase.
rows.action: Move to a safe reset location and heal that teammate. Use Great basic healing checks when they occur; do not assume a special check earns the same bonus.
rows.why: Do No Harm scales all three bonuses with the target's Hook States and only applies while healing another Survivor.

rows.situation: The injured target has no Hook States, the Killer contests the heal, or an urgent hook or generator needs coverage.
rows.action: Hand off the heal or return to the higher-value team job instead of chasing a perk activation.
rows.why: At zero target Hook States the perk has no bonus, and a denied heal consumes team tempo.

rows.situation: The heal is complete and the endangered teammate can take the next route.
rows.action: Separate into useful assignments; do not keep both players idle looking for another heal.
rows.why: The benefit is a restored teammate, not a standing team-wide buff.

abortWhen: Stop if Killer pressure makes the reset likely to cost a down.
Release the healer role when the target is no longer reachable or another teammate has the safe heal.

strengths: More healing value is concentrated on teammates closest to elimination.
weaknesses: Fresh-patch effectiveness remains provisional; low-hook-state targets and unsafe routes provide little return.
commonMistakes: Counting the healer's Hook States instead of the target's.
Assuming the Great-check bonus applies to non-basic checks or to self-healing.
